DNB pan-Baltic websites

Won a pan-Baltic tender and designed DNB’s websites and design system for three countries. After the merger with Nordea, Luminor kept our site as its platform.

Client
DNB Bank, now Luminor
Country
Latvia, Lithuania, Estonia
Industry
Banking
Year
2016–2020
My role
Project lead and UX lead
Team
A UI designer on the visuals; external developers built the sites

Problem

DNB needed new websites from scratch for Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia, in line with its strategy of fewer, clearer choices for customers.

  • Three countries, one consistent experience
  • External developers would build all three sites, including pages we never designed

Approach

Every decision traces back to evidence. Each step has an ID, and every insight and decision names the evidence it came from. The steps below are an example from this project.

  1. S001

    Source

    DNB’s strategy

    Fewer, clearer choices for customers.

  2. S002

    Source

    Stakeholder interviews

    In all three countries: Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia.

  3. S003

    Source

    Expert walkthrough

    The existing sites, page by page, along the main customer tasks.

  4. S004

    Source

    Heuristic evaluation

    A usability check of the existing sites against established heuristics.

  5. S005

    Source

    The developer setup

    External teams would build and extend all three sites.

  6. E001

    Evidence

    Too many products

    Five credit cards where two would do.

    From S001

  7. E002

    Evidence

    Mostly private customers

    The large majority of visitors are private customers.

    From S001, S002

  8. I001

    Insight

    Show less, one step at a time

    A calm page supports fewer, clearer choices.

    From S001, E001, S003, S004

  9. D001

    Decision

    Focused layouts

    Large calculators and full-screen elements revealed one by one while scrolling.

    From I001

  10. D002

    Decision

    Five cards became two

    The site supports the reduced range.

    From E001

  11. D003

    Decision

    Private by default

    Corporate clients switch over through the menu.

    From E002

  12. D004

    Decision

    A web style guide

    Every component, with code snippets, so developers can build new pages.

    From S005

Solution

I led the project and the UX, from the tender to the handoff. A UI designer did the visuals.

Three websites

We won the Latvian tender first, then the pan-Baltic final.

  • Minimalist, distraction-free layouts
  • Large calculators and full-screen elements revealed one by one while scrolling
  • Private customers as the default, corporate clients through a switch in the menu
  • 30+ page designs

Design system

A web style guide with all components and code snippets, so the developers could build pages the designs didn’t cover.

Outcome

Three countries now ran on one system of 30+ page designs, with five credit cards cut to two. After DNB and Nordea merged into Luminor, Luminor chose our DNB website as its platform and gave us the rebrand redesign. It is still in use. The handoff was smooth: developers built new pages from the system without major issues.
